triage.brief_framing: "Can you diagram modal-runtime for me? It keeps coming up and I don't have a clear picture of it."
questions_provoked: Q1 scope: the whole runtime, or one seam?
Q2 reader's job: what should the reader be able to answer from the picture?
Q5 is this a machine-manager diagram (the neighbouring case I already have)?
Q6 (made unnecessary by Q1): which components count as 'the runtime's internals' - all eight, or only the orchestration half?
Q7 (made unnecessary by Q2 and the source): should the worker pair be one bidirectional arrow or two directed ones?
Q8 (made unnecessary by Q4): slow sparse dots, or none?
Q9 (made unnecessary by Q1): do the historical qualifiers ('historical', 'unconfirmed') need dashed links?

questions_used.question: Scope: the whole runtime, or one seam?
questions_used.answer: All eight components and their eight relations - the seams, modules and RPCs. That's the point of the diagram.

questions_used.question: What is the reader's job?
questions_used.answer: I want to know which seam carries which protocol. The worker gRPC and the filesystem HTTP over UDS must not blur.

questions_used.question: Panes or one canvas?
questions_used.answer: One pane if the pair fits; a canvas with a described diagram per seam if the labels need room. Don't split just to make boxes smaller.

questions_used.question: Motion?
questions_used.answer: The source never shows motion - keep it static.

questions_used.question: Is this a machine-manager diagram?
questions_used.answer: No. It's the runtime's own internals; judge it by the runtime source, not by the machine-manager cases.

questions_used.question: Which label text do the two worker seams carry?
questions_used.answer: The source's own wording, verbatim: "task input + control RPCs" and "events + management RPCs". Annex answer 2 makes the ownership of these two strings the point, so they are not paraphrased on the canvas.
questions_used.reason: source.md's relationship facts name both strings; no annex answer may replace a source fact, and abbreviating them is exactly the blurring the reader forbade.

questions_used.question: Do any links need the uncertain (dashed) style?
questions_used.answer: No. source.md carries no 'unconfirmed'/'historical' qualifier on any of the eight relations, so every relation is drawn solid; the historical-chat caveat is provenance, not a qualifier on a link.
questions_used.reason: source.md marks the chat as evidence 'not authority to replay commands' but attaches no uncertainty to a relation; adding dashes would invent a qualifier.

questions_used.question: How are the eight boxes grouped by concept?
questions_used.answer: orchestration (modal-runtime, Task engine), compute (Container backend, Task container), storage (Filesystem + volumes, Blobnet); modal-worker and modal-daemon carry no group because they are boundary peers, not members of an internal cluster.
questions_used.reason: source.md's own summary line names 'task orchestration, container backends, storage, and three worker RPC seams'; the worker and the daemon are the two edge ends, so inventing a group for them would tidy the colours without a source fact.

triage.converged_when: After Q1-Q5 the picture was complete: scope = all eight components and eight relations; reader's job = which seam carries which protocol (so the pair must never blur and HTTP-over-UDS must not read as gRPC); shape = one pane if the anti-parallel pair fits, otherwise a described canvas; motion = none. Q6-Q9 were answered by Q1-Q4 and the source, so they were not asked again.

known_defects.detail: rataflow/src/main.rs prints 'warning: N label(s) needed a leader tick' whenever a label is placed via a leader tick (labels_leadered > 0). scripts/viz-validate.py's check_warnings_absent fails on any warning line except near-miss ones, so the round-13 leader-tick rescue cannot appear in a bundle that passes validation. Not triggered here (0 leader-ticked), but it removed the only one-view rescue for this case.

sections_extent() takes max(section.width), where section.width = max(drawing width, title length, description length), but each section's title/description is drawn at the section's x offset (dx). A description that is the widest element is therefore cut off at the canvas edge and cannot be panned into view. Measured: attempts/canvas-c3.json with a 163-char d3 description reported extent=163x34 and the drawn line ended '...filesystem HTTP on U' (recorded/canvas-full-dump.stdout line 27). Mitigation in the shipped spec: every description is 105 characters, drawn at x=22 inside a 133-wide canvas.

When the drawing area barely exceeds the canvas height the palette box is drawn over d3's bottom-left node. At COLUMNS=135 LINES=40 the box overwrites modal-runtime's left border (recorded/canvas-whole-135x40.stdout rows 36-37: '│ + [+]─│───────────╯'). At the natural pane (68x44) and the pinned 77x47 dump the palette sits below the drawing and no border is overwritten.

In d1 the two seam labels occupy adjacent rows between two short parallel runs (d1-section.txt rows 6-7). Ownership is structural (e0's label sits in a reserved label rank, e1's label was judged Own by the router) and --check reports 0 ambiguous owners, but a reader sees 'task input + control RPCs' one row above 'events + management RPCs' with both runs in view.

The pane is 68 columns, so d2's Task container and d3's Blobnet boxes fall outside the ANSI capture; their hues are asserted from the group accounting (groups: compute(2) storage(2)) rather than cited from pixels.

The shipped spec is canvas-c3 with descriptions shortened (label canvas-c3-final). That is a text-only revision of the third candidate: per-diagram extents, routes, ports and label placements are byte-identical to canvas-c3, so it is disclosed as a revision rather than counted as a fourth candidate in attempts.json.
